newsitem.title: UK: UK queen unveils memorial to civilian dead.
newsitem.headline: UK queen unveils memorial to civilian dead.

text.p: Britain's Queen Elizabeth, accompanied by survivors of the Holocaust and a Rwandan massacre, unveiled a memorial at London's Westminster Abbey to the innocent civilian victims of war and oppression.
The stone memorial bears the inscription "Remember All Innocent Victims of Oppression, Violence and War" and complements the Tomb of the Unknown Warrior, situated nearby in the Anglican Cathedral.

Also present were a teacher from Dunblane, the Scottish town where 16 children and their teacher were shot dead in March, and a 14-year-old Bosnian boy who lost both hands and his sight in the recent war in former Yugoslavia.

"Language stumbles and falls silent in face of the horror and the pity," said Michel Mayne, dean of the cathedral. "A few of you here have known such horror, the few representing the many, and we are silenced by your presence."

"This new stone speaks for those -- so many of them women and children -- who have been in the way: in the way of invading armies, pawns in a thousand messy wars," he told a congregation of several hundred, including 12 victims of war and oppression.
